root_cause.text: Missing validation of the `ErrorDataLength` field in `symlink_data()` allows integer arithmetic wrap-around on 32-bit architectures, leading to an infinite loop or out-of-bounds read when parsing SMB2 error responses.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly describes that when `p->ErrorDataLength` is `0xfffffff8` (aligned to 8), the pointer `next` equals `p`, causing an infinite loop; when `0xfffffff0`, `next` points before `p` by 8 bytes, causing an out-of-bounds read. The patch adds a bounds check (`if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p)))`) to prevent these conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary check to prevent out-of-bounds access when iterating over error context data in symlink response parsing.
intent_record.what: Added a check that verifies the aligned error data length does not exceed the remaining buffer space before advancing the pointer to the next error context entry.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now returns an error (-EINVAL) if the computed length would cause the pointer to go beyond the end of the buffer, preventing out-of-bounds memory access.
